Mr. Md. Zakir Hossain and Mr. Md. Ashraful Karim, Advocate ----- For the opposite party No.1
parties:
Md. Akther Hasan
Vs.
Md. Ruhul Amin Moral and another
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal, J : This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 9.12.2007 passed by the District Judge, Narayangonj in Misc. Appeal No.102 of 2007 dismissing the appeal summarily should not be set-aside. 

 2. Material facts of the case as necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj which was subsequently re-numbered on transfer as Title Suit No.279 of 2006. During the pendency of the suit for peremptory hearing the plaintiff petitioner could not attend before the Court on 31.7.2007 as a result of which the suit was dismissed for default. The plaintiff thereupon, filed Misc. Case No.12 of 2007 in the Court of Bandar Assistant Judge, Narayangonj for restoration of Title Suit No. 279 of 2006 after recalling the order of dismissal dated 31.7.2007. The learned Assistant Judge by his order dated 29.10.2007 rejected the Misc. Case. 

 3. Being unsuccessful, the petitioner preferred Misc. Appeal No.102 of 2007 before the learned District Judge, Naryangonj who by the impugned judgment and order dated 9.12.2007 dismissed the appeal summarily and the instant Revision application is directed against that judgment and order. 

 4. Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner submits that both the Courts below erred in law in rejecting the prayer for restoration of Title Suit No.279 of 2006 without properly considering the facts of the case and the case made out by the petitioner and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 9. On perusal of the record, it appears that the petitioner filed Misc. Case tinder Order IX, Rule 9 CPC for restoration of Title Suit No.279 of 2006 stating the ground that the plaintiff-petitioner was bedridden from 27.7.2007 to 12.09.2007 for the disease of hepatitis and thus he could not be present before the trial Court along with witnesses on 31.07.2007. 

 10. The trial Court below however by its order No.52 dated 29.10.2007 rejected the Misc. Case on the finding that: কিন্তু দেঃ মোঃ নং ২৭৯/০৬ এর ৪৮ নং আদেশ দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় যে, মোকদ্দমাটি পূর্বের C.P.Cost  দাখিল না করিয়া পুনরায় সময়ের প্রার্থনা করায় C.P.Cost দাখিল না করিবার কারনে মোকদ্দমা খারিজ করা হয়। কিন্তু অত্র ছানী মিসে দরখাস্তকারী পক্ষ ভিন্নরুপ বক্তব্য দিয়া ছানী মিস মোকদ্দমাটি আনয়ন করায় ইহা গ্রহনীয় নয় বলিয়া সিদ্ধান্ত গৃহীত হইল।” 

 The Court of appeal below in its turn disallowed the Misc. Appeal summarily by the impugned order dated 9.12.2007 holding that the trial Court below in the facts and circumstance of the case rightly disallowed the Misc. Case. 

 11. On scrutiny of the impugned judgment and order dated 9.12.2007 together with the order of the trial Court dated 29.10.2007 passed in Misc. Case No.12 of 2007 and order dated 31.7.2007 passed in Title Suit No. 279 of 2006, it appears that the Title Suit No.279 of 2006 was dismissed for default due to non-payment of C.P. cost of Tk.300/- rejecting the application for time and thereafter, the Misc. Case was disallowed on the ground that the plaintiff-petitioner took a different plea for restoring the Misc. Case. 

 12. On a reading of the application filed under Order IX, Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure together with the order dated 9.12.2007 and order of the trial Court dated 29.10.2007 and 31.7.2007, I am led to hold that in the facts and circumstance of the case both the Courts below ought to have given a chance to the petitioner to deposit C.P. cost of Tk. 300/- and in not doing so committed an error of law resulting in an error in the impugned decisions occasioning failure of justice. The Courts below committed wrong in not considering the attending circumstances and the case of the plaintiff-petitioner that he had sufficient cause for nonappearance in the suit when the suit was called on for hearing. Moreover, there being nothing on record to show that the plaintiff was negligent in pursuing the ease. I do not think therefore that both the Courts below made a correct approach to the simple problem. 

 15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned order dated 9.12.2007 passed in Misc. Appeal No.102 of 2007 is set-aside and consequently. Misc. Case No.12 of 2007 is allowed and the suit being Title Suit No.279 of 2006 is restored to its original file and number on condition that the plaintiff-petitioner shall deposit a sum of Tk. 25,000/- (twenty five thousand) as cost within 1 (one) month from the date of receipt of this order before the trial Court as prayed for.
